newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: RESEARCH ALERT-Jardine sees lower Sri Lankan rates.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Jardine sees lower Sri Lankan rates.

text.p: Brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB said a policy shift by Sri Lanka's Central Bank to raise money supply and cut rates augurs well for a sustained reduction in interest rates.
"It is our contention that the stage is now set for a sustained reduction in interest rates," the brokerage said in a report seen by Reuters on Wednesday.
The Central Bank has relaxed the statutory reserve requirement of commercial banks by three percent since January, releasing over five billion rupees into the system.

"Our forecast is for the prime lending rate to average at 16.7 percent in 1997 and 15.4 percent in 1998 and the Treasury Bill yield to average 15.25 and 14.26 percent in 1997 and 1998 respectively," the report said.
Relaxing statutory reserves signals more than a desire for lower interest rates. It reveals the surrendering of tight monetary policy held by the Central Bank for over five years, the report said.
Prime lending averaged 18.58 percent in 1996 while the benchmark 12-month Treasury Bill yield averaged 16.66.
Rates will climb in the second half in line with a cyclical pattern where they dip in the first half and pick up in the second, the report said
"However, we do not expect them to reach last year's levels as increased external inflows and lower government borrowing will cap upward pressure on the rates," it added.
